newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 13.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* Panamerican Beverages Inc has merged with Coca-Cola Hit de Venezuela.
* Fred Meyer Inc has agreed to acquire Smith's Food & Drug Centers Inc for about $700 million in stock.

* The European Commission's top antitrust official said a letter would be sent in a little over a week that outlines conditions Boeing Co must meet to win European approval for its bid to buy McDonnell Douglas Corp.
* The dollar fell against the yen, reaching its lowest level in nearly four months. The dollar rose against the German mark.
* Citrix Systems Inc's stock rose after Microsoft Corp said it had agreed to license its software technology.
* Occidental Petroleum Corp said it had implemented tighter internal controls for its dealings with foreign governments and businessmen.
* Paxson Communications Corp has agreed to acquire WBIS+, a New York television station, from Dow Jones & Co Inc and ITT Corp.
* The editor of the San Jose Mercury News acknowledged that a series of articles on crack cocaine in urban America, which sparked a number of federal investigations, was marred by shortcomings.
* The rise in coffee prices in the futures market has trickled down to the retail arena, making for more expensive cups of coffee.
* Apple Computer Inc plans to demonstrate an early version of its new operating system software.
* Delta Air Lines Inc Chairman, Chief Executive and President Ronald Allen said he plans to retire this summer.
* The Dow Jones Industrial average and the Standard & Poor's Index of 500 stocks both increased by more than 1.5 percent and reached closing highs.
* Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc have agreed to merge in a deal worth about $22.27 billion.
* The planned merger of Grand Metropolitan and Guinness brings together brings together two companies that have been fighting for a shrinking share of the alcohol-consuming public.
